run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:23:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a configuration change in the checkout Deployment. At 2026-11-16T16:32:31Z the checkout Deployment rolled out a new ReplicaSet, checkout-849d65649b, whose pod template sets KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999, whereas the previous ReplicaSet, checkout-5dccddf8bb, used kafka:9092 with the same image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout. The cluster Service kafka exposes only 9092 (plaintext) and 9093 (controller) on ClusterIP 100.66.162.182, so the new pod's Kafka producer cannot connect: it logs dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout and kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to, then terminates with reason Error and exit code 2 and enters BackOff. Checkout's PlaceOrder therefore fails; frontend's grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder client spans and its /api/checkout route spans carry about 327 error spans in the window while every other frontend operation has zero errors, and frontend-proxy's Envoy access log shows POST /api/checkout returning 500 via_upstream with upstream frontend. frontend-proxy ingress error spans rose from zero to about 0.83 spans per second from roughly 16:35, which is what the alert measures. Kafka itself was checked and is not the failing component: the kafka pod is Running and ready with zero restarts, and the accounting Deployment, still configured with kafka:9092, consumed about 396 order spans with zero errors in the same window.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emitted error spans concentrated in the 16:23:53 to 16:46:53Z window: span_name ingress with STATUS_CODE_ERROR increased 338.83 versus STATUS_CODE_UNSET 12549.06, and span_name router frontend egress with STATUS_CODE_ERROR increased 328.53 versus 12559.36. Viewed as a per-second rate of ingress spans, the error series was 0 from 16:23:53 through about 16:32 and then climbed to 0.33, 0.74, 0.82, 0.87, 0.66, 0.87, 0.91 in the minutes to 16:45.

The errors are specific to the checkout path. In the same window the frontend service had error-span increases of 327.36 on span POST, 327.36 on POST /api/checkout, 327.50 on executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and 327.50 on grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, while GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds all increased by 0 error spans; frontend tcp.connect also showed 36.05 error spans. Across all services the only other nonzero error increases were long-lived stream spans: ad and fraud-detection flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 2.06 each and recommendation /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.03.

frontend's gRPC client operation grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder shows the onset: STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate was 0 through 16:32:53, 0.173 at 16:33:53, 0.427 at 16:34:53 and about 0.70 to 0.77 per second from 16:35:53 onward, while STATUS_CODE_UNSET calls fell from about 0.79 to 0.89 per second before 16:32 to 0 from 16:36:53 on.

frontend-proxy's own access log records the user-visible failures on the checkout route, repeatedly logging POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1 500 with via_upstream and upstream frontend between 16:39:20 and 16:40:57, while other routes such as GET /api/products continue to return 200; 932 log lines matched the 500, error or checkout filter inside the window.

The checkout Deployment rolled out a new ReplicaSet at 16:32:31Z: event Scaled up replica set checkout-849d65649b from 0 to 1 on Deployment checkout, SuccessfulCreate Created pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz, and scaledown and SuccessfulDelete of checkout-5dccddf8bb with pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8 at 16:32:34Z.

The pod template changed only the Kafka address: ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb, created 15:59:13Z with replicas 0, sets env KAFKA_ADDR to kafka:9092, while ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b, created 16:32:31Z with replicas 1, sets env KAFKA_ADDR to kafka:9999; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout and their listed env vars for cart, currency, payment, product-catalog, shipping, email, flagd and OTEL are otherwise identical.

The Service kafka in namespace otel-demo, ClusterIP 100.66.162.182 with selector opentelemetry.io/name kafka, exposes only ports 9092 named plaintext and 9093 named controller; it defines no port 9999.

Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz runs container checkout with env KAFKA_ADDR set to kafka:9999 and is crash-looping: the container lastState terminated with reason Error and exitCode 2 finishedAt 16:36:09Z, and its current state is also terminated with reason Error and exitCode 2, startedAt 16:36:10Z and finishedAt 16:39:36Z; restartCount is 1, ready is false, and a Warning event Back-off restarting failed container checkout at 16:39:37Z was recorded. The Deployment reports replicas 1, updatedReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 and no readyReplicas.

The checkout container logs name the failing dependency port exactly: Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout, client/metadata no available broker to send metadata request to, and kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout; the effective service config prints kafkaBrokerSvcAddr as kafka:9999 with KafkaProducerClient nil. The sequence repeats from 16:33:03Z to 16:40:51Z on each restart; at 16:36:09Z a PlaceOrder reached the PlaceOrder log line and payment went through before the Kafka producer initialisation failed and the process exited.

The pod init container wait-for-kafka, image busybox:latest, only waits for kafka port 9092 with the command until nc -z -v -w30 kafka 9092; do echo waiting for kafka; sleep 2; done, so pod startup succeeds even though the application container is pointed at kafka:9999.

Kafka was checked and is not the failing component: pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running, ready true, with 0 restarts and started 15:59:12Z, and its container logs show normal broker and KRaft activity such as segment rolls and snapshots between 16:39:45Z and 16:40:51Z. Another client keeps working against the same broker: pod accounting-58d4b6c958-rmc4p uses KAFKA_ADDR kafka:9092 and in the window produced 396.50 orders receive spans with 0 error spans, 396.50 STATUS_CODE_OK otel spans and 396.50 order-consumed spans.

frontend-proxy itself is up and serving: pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c is Running with ready true and 0 restarts, and its Envoy log shows successful 200 responses on other routes, for example GET /api/products and GET /, interleaved with the 500s whose upstream is recorded as frontend with via_upstream.

Deepest supported cause: the checkout Deployment pod template was changed to set KAFKA_ADDR to kafka:9999, a port the kafka Service does not expose. Checkout's Sarama producer therefore times out against the Service ClusterIP with dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout, the container exits with code 2 and enters BackOff, PlaceOrder calls from frontend fail, frontend returns 500 on /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy ingress spans turn STATUS_CODE_ERROR, which is what the RequestErrorRate warning measures.

Alternative candidate considered and not supported: a defect in the checkout image or application code rather than configuration. The same image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout was serving successful PlaceOrder calls, with frontend PlaceOrder STATUS_CODE_UNSET about 0.8 per second, until 16:32:53Z from the ReplicaSet configured with kafka:9092, and failures begin only with the ReplicaSet that sets kafka:9999, so the observable change is configuration rather than image content.

Rejected: the kafka broker or pod was down or overloaded. The kafka pod is Running and ready with 0 restarts, its logs show active broker work through 16:40:51Z, and accounting continued consuming orders over kafka:9092 with zero errors while checkout failed; the checkout error names port 9999, which the kafka Service does not publish at all.

Restore the checkout Deployment KAFKA_ADDR to the value the kafka Service actually publishes, kafka:9092, as in ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb, and roll the Deployment; the address is a plain env literal in the pod template rather than a Secret, so no secret value needs to be read.

Add a readiness or liveness check on the checkout container that exercises Kafka connectivity, or align the wait-for-kafka init container with KAFKA_ADDR, since the init container only checks kafka:9092 while the application needs kafka:9999 and the container currently crash-loops while the init gate passes.

gaps: The alert's own expression and the meaning of the reported value 1.7333 could not be verified: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no_data (view d08b59b7-ed53-4478-a709-83bdad9246aa-t0:4eb13113-a1d6-45dc-9080-c4f3cb157261), so no rule with that exact name existed in the loaded rules at query time.

The alert start 2026-11-16T16:23:53Z precedes the observed error onset at about 16:33:53Z, after the 16:32:31Z checkout rollout; which series produced the alert value before that onset, and whether the alert timestamp is reliable, remain unknown.

Change history is not an available integration, so who or what edited the checkout Deployment KAFKA_ADDR, and the exact change object, could not be verified; only the resulting ReplicaSet difference and its 16:32:31Z creation time are observed.

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend-proxy and none with error tag true for frontend in the window (views db947f40-176e-4f71-aa10-3cffb1bf9b7d-t1:9de90584-186b-4d0d-987a-490279061185 and 6c15f397-71b1-4e16-b3c2-ba8d01454b07-t0:3ca57ff9-06ed-4aa4-bbf4-43beff591014, both no_data), so trace-level parent-child propagation from frontend to checkout could not be confirmed from spans; the conclusions rest on metrics and proxy access logs.

gRPC latency metric series were absent: the queries against rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_count and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and the metric-name lookup for rpc_.* all returned no_data (views 62b15751-8825-4380-9ca5-ea1f0ee1a4e7-t1:73e57125-3a75-472c-b296-709c2cc6b6bb, 62b15751-8825-4380-9ca5-ea1f0ee1a4e7-t2:4c3f5484-b461-45e6-a725-5c28990309e5 and 6c15f397-71b1-4e16-b3c2-ba8d01454b07-t1:3f220146-e682-448e-9d5e-14bed65e961b, all no_data), so gRPC status-code labels could not be inspected and the absence of those series is unknown rather than zero.

Image digests were not compared: both ReplicaSets carry the same image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout, so a change of image content under the same tag cannot be excluded from the evidence gathered.

Log coverage was partial: the checkout container view was incomplete with only the newest 60 of 826 matching lines shown (e35dcad7-dee1-4002-afee-d384efbd8808-t2:26834ad1-6e79-4fad-815c-db2846f8496e) and the frontend-proxy view was incomplete with the newest 80 of 932 matching lines shown (d255aa5e-a1bc-40aa-a4f5-e84f2b956619-t1:5a3441d9-7436-4f9a-9841-38ef868ae632); the frontend pod produced no readable log lines in the window (view d255aa5e-a1bc-40aa-a4f5-e84f2b956619-t0:308cf59d-d99a-4fc0-8116-f00eb6432c79, no_data), and no previous container instance logs existed, so older instances of the failure remain unknown.

Kafka pod state and Kubernetes object readings are point-in-time snapshots taken after the window and cannot prove the exact cluster state during 16:23 to 16:46Z, although the Service port list, which contains no 9999, is the operative fact.
Downstream or customer impact beyond the observed 500 responses on /api/checkout was not measured.
next_steps: Correct KAFKA_ADDR in the checkout Deployment to kafka:9092, or publish port 9999 on the kafka Service if that is intentional, then verify the checkout pod stays Ready without restarts and that frontend PlaceOrder error spans return to zero.
Retrieve the checkout Deployment change record or revision from change history to identify the author and time of the KAFKA_ADDR edit.
Confirm the alert's actual query and threshold from the Alertmanager and Prometheus rule source, and reconcile the 16:23:53Z alert start with the roughly 16:33 onset.
Align a dependency-aware startup or readiness check for checkout so a Kafka address mismatch fails pod readiness instead of surfacing as 500 responses at the ingress.
